A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three prototype galectins in the chicken are not only different in their expression patterns, but also show marked differences in their structure and their interaction with lactose.

the fine-tuning of galectin structures and functions is achieved through a delicate balance between the conservation and the modulation of the structural and functional properties of the prototypic galectins.
the chicken galectins are fine-tuned to perform different tasks, with CG-2 having a more restricted range than CG-1A or CG-1B.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the high degree of sequence conservation, the galectins of chicken are fine-tuned to a high extent, which is a hallmark of their biological role.

the fine-tuning of the galectin family in chicken is achieved by subtle structural modifications that affect the hydrodynamic behaviour, the stability, the dimer interface, the carbohydrate-binding site and the trimerization mode.

the galectin family is not only characterized by a large diversity of structures and functions, but also by a remarkable plasticity in the way these lectins are fine-tuned to fulfil their roles in the living organism.
